reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 17 --verse 1.124.2: the evidence stands verbatim in Sayana's commentary on 1.124.2 (daivyani vratani devasambandhini agnihotradini karmani ... aminati ahimsanti bhanapradanenanukulam kurvati ... manusyanam yugani ... pramnati prakarsena himsanti ayuh ksapayantityarthah) and carries the whole reading: the gods' rites such as the Agnihotra, which she does not harm but makes favourable by giving light, and the life of men, which she wears away. He offers a second reading of yugani (pairs she separates); choosing his first is not drift. Wilson's 1.124.2 and note (not opposing, the fit season of the rites) follow him. Plain sense: day.js shows 1.124.1 with the fire kindled and Savitar sending each quadruped and biped to labour; Dawn's dealings with men recur in 1.124.6, 7, 10 and 12, with the gods in 1.124.2 to 3. 'The hymn weighs' leans on verse 2 but does not claim more than the hymn holds; no four-word run of the key. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.124.2, at [123,2]); entry-check ok, no warns. No school needed, no comparison, tone plain.
